title: From Pep Guardiola's Salary to the National Minimum Wage: How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert any hourly rate to annual pay, from Pep Guardiola's salary to the National Minimum Wage. Includes tax, super, casual loading, and fortnightly amounts.
salarySummary: Using the standard 38-hour week, annual pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour, giving $1,004.90/week or $52,254.80/year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a 38-hour week, that's hourly × 38 × 52. For a 40-hour week, use your actual hours. The result is annual gross before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does the National Minimum Wage include casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour for award/agreement-free employees. Casual employees get a 25% loading on top, making it $33.05/hour. Always enter the base rate; the calculator adds loading separately.

faqs.q: What tax and super should I expect?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, tax is nil up to $18,200; 15% to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above. Medicare levy is 2%. Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings paid on top, capped at $270,830. These are estimates, not a determination.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Pay

Whether you're curious about **Pep Guardiola's salary** or your own rate, the conversion is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For most full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This gives a simple annual figure before tax, super, and other deductions.

## The Basic Formula

Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a 38‑hour week, that's hourly × 38 × 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80 per year. If you work 40 hours, use 40 instead. The formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice.

### Why 38 Hours?

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage based on a 38‑hour week. Most modern awards also use 38 hours for full‑time work. If your contract or award says otherwise, use your ordinary hours. Part‑time and casual employees can use their average weekly hours.

### Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. Multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the National Minimum Wage: $1,004.90 per week × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight before tax. This helps when budgeting or comparing salary offers.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This applies to award/agreement‑free employees. Most employees are covered by an award, which sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman reports that award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026. Always check your specific award using the [pay guides](/blog) or the [reference tables](/data) on this site.

For context, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (May 2026) reports full‑time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week. That's about $54.83 per hour for a 38‑hour week – well above the minimum. The all‑employees total earnings figure of $1,579.20 per week includes part‑time workers, showing the range of ordinary‑time earnings across the workforce.

## Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that's $26.44 + 25% = $33.05 per hour. When using the [timesheet](/) on this site, enter your base hourly rate (without loading) and check the casual loading box. The calculator adds 25% automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes loading.

## Superannuation and Tax

Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For the National Minimum Wage, that's $52,254.80 × 12% = $6,270.58 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an extra contribution by your employer.

Tax for 2026–27 uses the resident scale: tax‑free threshold up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above. Medicare levy is generally 2%. The [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator on this site uses these rates, but note that the Medicare reduction thresholds for singles are from 2025–26, as 2026–27 figures were not confirmed at the time of this estimate.

## Putting It All Together

To estimate your annual pay, start with your hourly rate and hours per week. Multiply to get weekly, then annual. Add super (12% on top) and subtract estimated tax and Medicare. For example, a full‑time worker on the National Minimum Wage:

- Hourly: $26.44
- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Annual: $52,254.80
- Super (12%): $6,270.58
- Tax (approx): $7,867 (using 2026‑27 rates)
- Medicare (2%): $1,045.10
- Net annual: $43,342.70

This is an estimate. Actual pay depends on your award, allowances, penalty rates, and whether you salary sacrifice. For more detail, see the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) pages.

## Conclusion

Whether you're comparing **Pep Guardiola's salary** (reportedly in the tens of millions per year) or your own rate, the same formula applies: hourly × hours × 52. The key is knowing your ordinary hours and whether you're award‑free or covered by an award. Use the [timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures, and always check the Fair Work Ombudsman for your specific award. Remember, super is paid on top, and tax is deducted from your gross pay. For casual workers, the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how the 25% loading works. For job‑specific rates, visit [job pay](/topics/job-pay).

This site provides estimates, not determinations. For precise advice, consult a qualified professional or your employer.
